note: The masjid's own story, rendered by history.html. Same rule as events.json: a milestone is only published as fact with a 'source' saying how we know it. Entries with "status": "unknown" are deliberate gaps - questions for the people who were there - and they render as open questions rather than facts. When one is answered, give it a year, a source, set status to confirmed and delete its 'asks' list. Every 'source' must be something that can be checked: the Charity Commission register or the charity's filed accounts, Companies House, HM Land Registry, the masjid's own posts, or the masjid's own archive (its letters, notices, programmes and letterheads from 2004 onwards, kept privately by the masjid). Nothing from the archive's personal records, accounts, leases, rents or fundraising figures is published: see 'Our Story' in CLAUDE.md. 'chapter' places a milestone in one of the chapters listed in 'chapters', in file order. Optional 'image', 'image_alt', 'image_width' and 'image_height' show a photograph in the card (or under a chapter's opening), 'image_caption' says where and when it was taken, and 'image_fit': 'contain' shows a logo whole on a plain panel instead of cropping it. Never a photo of an identifiable child. 'strand' is one of: charity, building, learning, community.

chapters.title: Garrison Lane
chapters.intro: The story starts in Bordesley Green, at the Garrison Centre on Garrison Lane: first a madrasah, then a charity, then a masjid named after it.
chapters.image_alt: The Garrison Centre on Garrison Lane: red-brick Victorian buildings with tall arched windows, a chimney and a red gate, under a blue sky
chapters.image_caption: The Garrison Centre, 106 Garrison Lane. From the masjid's archive.

chapters.title: Revesby Walk
chapters.intro: Before it was ours, 2 Revesby Walk was a social club. In 2019 the charity took it on, and over the next three years turned it into a masjid.
chapters.image_alt: The masjid's red-brick building on Revesby Walk under a blue sky, its sign above the entrance canopy

chapters.title: Today
chapters.intro: The five daily prayers and Jumu'ah, Madrasah Al Furqan's five groups, conferences and courses, and a record the masjid now keeps in public.
chapters.image_alt: The masjid at dusk, its sign lit above the entrance

milestones.title: Al Furqan comes to Garrison Lane
milestones.body: The madrasah is older than the masjid. In December 2004 Madrasah Al Furqan moves into the Garrison Centre, 106 Garrison Lane in Bordesley Green, with a few classes and about 50 children. SOS Education Organisation, which ran the centre, called it the first department created there. By the summer of 2006 it was teaching in two groups.
asks: Where did Al Furqan teach before it moved to Garrison Lane, and when did it begin?
milestones.source: SOS Education Organisation's description of the Garrison Centre, and the madrasah's own notices from 2006. Both are in the masjid's archive.
milestones.image_alt: An earlier logo of Madrasah Al Furqan: an open Qur'an on a wooden stand inside a yellow circle, with the name in Arabic beneath
milestones.image_caption: An earlier Al Furqan logo, from the madrasah's own files.

milestones.title: The charity is founded
milestones.body: A Declaration of Trust dated 3 September 2006 sets up the charity as the Somali Education and Cultural Centre. Its first purpose is the advancement of Islam, alongside education, the relief of poverty and sickness, and recreation for the community.
milestones.source: Charity Commission register, charity 1142204: governing document and previous names.

milestones.title: A masjid at Garrison Lane
milestones.body: In January 2007 a masjid opens at the Garrison Centre, 'by demand of the local community and the centre's service users': Masjid Dar al-Tarbiya. The name, and today's Attarbiya, come from the charity's own Arabic name, Dar al-Tarbiya wal-Thaqafa al-Somaliya: the House of Education and Somali Culture.
asks: Who led the first prayers at Garrison Lane?
Is January 2007 right? If you remember the first Jumu'ah there, tell us.
milestones.source: SOS Education Organisation's description of the Garrison Centre, and the charity's own letterhead, which gives its name in Arabic. Both are in the masjid's archive.
milestones.image_alt: The prayer hall at Garrison Lane: a wooden mihrab and minbar above green prayer carpet
milestones.image_caption: The prayer hall at Garrison Lane, November 2012.

milestones.title: The first youth conference
milestones.body: On 16 April 2011 the masjid and Al Furqan hold their first youth conference at the Garrison Centre: Islamic lectures in English, with two guest speakers from London.
milestones.source: The conference's own programme, in the masjid's archive.

milestones.title: A registered charity
milestones.body: On 2 June 2011 the Charity Commission registers the charity, with the number it still carries: 1142204.

milestones.title: One school
milestones.body: From 1 July 2012 the masjid's own school, Daru Tarbiya, and Al Furqan become one school with one administration. Parents were told on 24 June. Al Furqan has been the masjid's madrasah ever since.
milestones.source: The notice to parents of 24 June 2012, in the masjid's archive.
milestones.image_alt: A long corridor at the Garrison Centre with shoes lined up along both walls
milestones.image_caption: Shoes along a corridor at the Garrison Centre, November 2012.

milestones.title: Ramadan at Garrison Lane
milestones.body: The masjid's Ramadan programme: tafsir of the Qur'an every day, iftar together, tarawih and i'tikaf. On 18 August 2012 the community was invited to 106 Garrison Lane to celebrate the completion of the tafsir, and the completion in 2013 was filmed.
milestones.source: The masjid's Ramadan programme, its invitation to the completion of the tafsir in 2012, and a film of the 2013 completion. All are in the masjid's archive.

milestones.title: The Al-Kownayn Centre
milestones.body: By June 2014 the centre at Garrison Lane has a new name and logo: the Al-Kownayn Centre, home of Masjid Dar-Attarbiyah and Madrassa Al-Furqan, the masjid and the madrasah under one name. It is the earliest use we have found of the name the charity is registered under today, Kowneyn Education and Cultural Centre.
asks: When did the charity choose the name Kowneyn, and what does it mean to the people who chose it?
milestones.source: The centre's logo and letterhead, June 2014, in the masjid's archive. The registered name: the Charity Commission register.
milestones.image_alt: The Al-Kownayn Centre logo: a masjid and an open book in a blue oval, ringed by the words Masjid Dar-Attarbiyah and Madrassa Al-Furqan in English and Arabic

milestones.title: The Garrison Lane years
milestones.body: For most of its life the masjid was at the Garrison Centre, 106 Garrison Lane in Bordesley Green, the community the charity was set up to serve. From April 2007 the charity used rooms there under a licence from SOS Education Organisation, which held the centre's lease from Birmingham City Council. It held the five daily prayers, the madrasah's classes, Ramadan tafsir and tarawih, and organised Eid prayers in Garrison Lane park. The charity's accounts give the Garrison Centre as its principal office up to the year ending March 2022. From the following year it is 2 Revesby Walk.
asks: Who remembers the move to Nechells, and the last prayer at Garrison Lane?
Do you have photographs of the Garrison Centre, inside or out?
milestones.source: The charity's annual accounts, 2021/22 and 2022/23, filed with the Charity Commission. The 2007 licence, the masjid's appeals and its letters from 2012 to 2014, in the masjid's archive.
milestones.image_alt: The main building of the Garrison Centre on a grey day: twin gables with round windows, tall arched windows and purple doors
milestones.image_caption: The Garrison Centre's main building, January 2014, from a film of the centre.

milestones.title: Before the club
milestones.body: How long the club was on Revesby Walk, and what the building was before it, is not written down anywhere we can check. Many people remember a pub on the street: that was the Ashted Hamlet, which stood on Revesby Walk from 1966 to 1997 and was later demolished. It was a different building from the masjid.
asks: When was the building built, and who for?
Was the club ever called the East Birmingham Constitutional Club, the 'Conservative club' at the top of Revesby Walk?
Do you have photographs of the club, inside or out?
milestones.source: Ashted Hamlet: closedpubs.co.uk and the Birmingham History Forum. The 'Conservative club' at the top of Revesby Walk: a 2005 post on the Birmingham History Forum.

milestones.title: The Vauxhall Sports and Social Club
milestones.body: Before it was a masjid, 2 Revesby Walk was a social club. A community interest company for the Vauxhall Sports and Social Club was registered at this address from October 2007 until it was dissolved in June 2010.
milestones.source: Companies House, company 06409217. The masjid's earlier website also describes the building as the former home of the Vauxhall Sports and Social Club.

milestones.title: 2 Revesby Walk becomes ours
milestones.body: In June 2019 the building at 2 Revesby Walk changes hands, and from then on the charity's accounts list land and buildings of exactly the price that was paid. This is the turning point of the whole story.
asks: Who made it happen, and how was the money raised?
What state was the building in when we got the keys?
milestones.source: HM Land Registry price paid record for 2 Revesby Walk, 14 June 2019, and the charity's balance sheets from 2020/21 onwards.

milestones.title: Becoming a masjid
milestones.body: Turning a club into a place of worship: the prayer hall and its carpet, the wudu area, and the marble wall around the mihrab and minbar. The charity's accounts record substantial spending on repairs and renewals to the building in each of the three years from April 2020 to March 2023.
asks: What was built or refitted, and in what order?
Are there photographs from during the work?
milestones.source: The charity's annual accounts, 2020/21 to 2022/23, filed with the Charity Commission.
milestones.image_alt: The mihrab and minbar today, set in a white and gold marble wall above red carpet

milestones.title: The first prayer
milestones.body: The first salah prayed in the building. Someone remembers this. It belongs at the centre of this page.
asks: When was the first prayer held here?
Who led it, and how many people came?

milestones.title: A new chapter on paper
milestones.body: The charity's Declaration of Trust is amended on 5 March 2021. Today it is registered as Kowneyn Education and Cultural Centre, and its earlier names on the register include Somali Education and Cultural Centre. The community knows it as Attarbiya Masjid.
milestones.source: Charity Commission register: governing document amended 5 March 2021; registered name and previous names.

milestones.title: The first Winter Conference on record
milestones.body: Three days on the lives of the Sahabah, from 29 to 31 December 2023, with talks after Jumu'ah, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. A second, a one-day seminar, followed in January 2025.
milestones.source: The masjid's own conference poster and timetable. See the events page.

milestones.title: The masjid goes online
milestones.body: The masjid starts publishing its own record. The first Instagram post, welcoming people to the masjid's official page, is on 18 March 2024, and the YouTube channel follows on 21 March. Almost everything on our events page is evidenced by these two accounts.
milestones.source: First post date from the masjid's Instagram account; channel creation date from YouTube's own feed.

milestones.title: Al Kissaii, for the teenagers
milestones.body: The masjid's programme for teenagers and older children, which runs the youth nights.
asks: What year did Al Kissaii start, and who started it?

milestones.title: A summer of Qur'an
milestones.body: A Qur'an Intensive Course for under-16s runs from 21 July to 24 August 2025, Monday to Thursday: hifdh, the fiqh of salah, basic Arabic reading and Islamic studies.
milestones.source: The masjid's Instagram, 13 July 2025. See the events page.

milestones.title: Five prayers, every day
milestones.body: Daily prayers and Jumu'ah, the Al Furqan madrasah, lessons and conferences, youth nights and Eid. The timetable is published live on this site and the programme is on the events page.
milestones.source: Prayer times come from the masjid's own Masjidbox timetable; events are evidenced one by one on the events page.
milestones.image_alt: Brothers standing in rows for Dhuhr in the main prayer hall, seen from behind
milestones.image_caption: Dhuhr in the main prayer hall, October 2026.
